title: perf bench latency-throughput scratchpad
content:
Quick scratchpad for latency/throughput runs (personal notes).
Owner: Priya Desai
Context: measuring p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec for small-medium sequence workloads to validate batching & KV cache heuristics for Dedicated GPU pool.

Experiment setup:
- HW: g4dn-type cluster (4x A10G) — single serving-node runs (1 GPU) for isolated numbers.
- Model: llama-13b variant (redwood-13b-v1), two precision modes: fp16 (baseline) and int8 (quantized).
- Seq lengths tested: 128, 512, 1024 (mostly 512).
- Batch sizes: 1, 4, 8, 16
- KV cache: on/off (cache warm runs vs cold)
- Warmup: 1000 tokens warmup for each config, then 10k tokens measured (aggregated across requests)
- Metrics captured: p50/p95/p99 latency per request (ms), tokens/sec (throughput), GPU util %, memory usage (MB)
- Notes: request size = prompt 32 tokens + gen 64 tokens typical; throughput measured as generated tokens/sec.

Run logs (selected):
1) fp16, seq=512, batch=1, kv=off
- p50: 72 ms, p95: 180 ms, p99: 320 ms
- tokens/sec: 95 tok/s
- gpu mem: 22.4 GB, gpu util ~58%
- notes: baseline single request latency good; high p99 due to scheduling jitter

2) fp16, seq=512, batch=4, kv=off
- p50: 110 ms, p95: 240 ms, p99: 420 ms
- tokens/sec: 320 tok/s
- gpu mem: 23.1 GB, gpu util ~78%
- notes: throughput improves ~3.3x vs batch=1, latency tradeoff as expected

3) fp16, seq=512, batch=8, kv=off
- p50: 210 ms, p95: 360 ms, p99: 650 ms
- tokens/sec: 560 tok/s
- gpu util: ~92% (approaching saturation)
- notes: diminishing returns beyond batch=8 for this model on this hw

4) int8, seq=512, batch=4, kv=off
- p50: 95 ms, p95: 210 ms, p99: 360 ms
- tokens/sec: 430 tok/s
- gpu mem: 16.8 GB, gpu util ~80%
- notes: int8 improves tokens/sec ~30% with lower memory footprint; int8 p99 slightly better vs fp16 for same batch

5) fp16, seq=512, batch=4, kv=on (cache warm)
- p50: 65 ms, p95: 120 ms, p99: 180 ms
- tokens/sec: 520 tok/s
- notes: KV cache gives big p95/p99 wins for repeated prefixes — as expected for chat-like workloads

6) int8, seq=512, batch=4, kv=on
- p50: 58 ms, p95: 105 ms, p99: 160 ms
- tokens/sec: 670 tok/s
- notes: best overall throughput+latency when combining int8 + kv cache for warm sessions

Cold vs warm cache impact (fp16, batch=4):
- cold p95: ~240 ms, warm p95: ~120 ms => ~2x improvement
- cold tokens/sec: 320, warm tokens/sec: 520 => ~60% improvement

Sequence length sensitivity (fp16, batch=4, kv=off):
- seq=128: p50 65 ms, tokens/sec 420 tok/s
- seq=512: p50 110 ms, tokens/sec 320 tok/s
- seq=1024: p50 220 ms, tokens/sec 180 tok/s
-> throughput roughly inversely proportional to seq length due to attention costs; kernel selection matters here

Cost math quick (very rough):
- baseline fp16 batch=4 tokens/sec 320. Assuming $X per GPU-hour => unit token cost = (GPU-hour-cost)/(tokens per hour).
- int8 + kv warm best-case reduces unit token cost by ~2.1x vs fp16 cold single-request baseline (approx). Need proper accounting in billing model later.

Observations / quick conclusions:
- KV cache is the single most impactful lever for p95/p99 for conversational workloads with repeated prefixes.
- Quantization (int8) is a strong win for throughput and memory; stability looks OK for redwood-13b-v1 in these runs but need regression tests on quality (evals) before recommending broadly.
- For latency-sensitive single-request workloads, keep batch size small (1-2). For throughput/throughput-cost optimization, batch 4-8 is sweet spot on A10G for this model.
- p99 outliers often correlate with CPU scheduling spikes or memcpy stalls; need deeper tracing (perf counters + nvprof) on p99 samples.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Run same matrix on A100-like instance to compare kernel perf (scheduling differences).
- Expand to longer gen lengths (256/512 gen) to see interaction with kv cache and kv memory scaling.
- Validate int8 on eval set (ROUGE/BLEU/LL-level) vs fp16 to quantify quality delta.
- Add automated harness entry in infra repo (github link above) to produce standardized CSV outputs + small charts.
- Investigate p99 sources: attach perf traces for top 10 p99 requests, correlate with node-level CPU spikes.

Temporary checklist:
- [ ] Add A100 run to matrix (owner: Ethan)
- [ ] Hook CSV exporter into perf harness (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Run int8 quality eval on evalset-v2 (owner: Samira)
- [ ] Create perf dashboard tile for kv cache impact (owner: Alex)

Notes for writeup: include simple table and two charts: 1) tokens/sec vs batch size (for fp16/int8), 2) p95 vs batch size (with kv on/off). Placeholder charts below for quick reference:

References: JIRA-2345 contains the end-to-end plan for rollout heuristics. PR #879 has the kv caching refactor — use that commit hash when reproducing tests.

Last notes: keep this doc as scratchpad; will convert to a cleaned perf-run report once A100 numbers plus int8 quality check are in.

End of scratchpad.
